context:
Goal: a change to this page reaches you only the way you want, and the page stops waiting on questions you have already answered.
Problem (rule): you ruled on 29 Oct that the page is rebuilt on main's newest code without being asked. Your goal for this session added a hold: the page writer republishes only fixes you asked for until you say how a page change is approved. Three page changes are queued behind merges (#3543 the recommendation and Waiting-on lines, #3469 the page link in chat, and the republish after them). Only you can lift or keep the hold, because it sets what shows on your own page.
Based on (ruling): wp-republish-on-template (owner, 2026-10-29 14:47 CDT): the waiting page is rebuilt on main's newest code without being asked, in every repo.
Based on (read): your goal for this session: republish only fixes you asked for until you answer.
Departs from: main republishes every merged page change and sends no message (ruling wp-republish-on-template) — b adds one line with a link after each republish, a holds every change for your yes.
Waiting on: you; until you answer I republish only fixes you asked for.
home: step page-recommend-and-waiting-on (draft PR #3543) and the page republish procedure, skills/waiting-page/reference/republish.md

options.gain: You see each change before it goes live.
options.how: The writer republishes a merged page change only after you say yes to that change.
options.label: Keep the hold: every page change waits for your word before the page is republished
options.lose: The page can lag merged changes for hours or days, and you answer one more question each time.

options.gain: Your asks land fast, and you still hear about every change.
options.how: The writer republishes after every merged page change, as on 29 Oct, and sends you one line with the link naming what changed.
options.label: Lift the hold: republish every merged page change, and send you one line with a link saying what changed
options.lose: A change you did not ask for can go live before you have looked at it.

options.how: The writer republishes after every merged page change, as on 29 Oct, and sends nothing else.
options.label: Lift the hold with no message: republish every merged page change and say nothing
options.lose: You may find a change only by looking at the page.

title: Since your hold on page changes you did not ask for, should the page go back to republishing every merged change, with a link line, or stay on hold?
why: It goes back to your 29 Oct rule and keeps you told about each change, so the page stops lagging.
